records.title: Few-Shot Defect Image Generation via Defect-Aware Feature Manipulation

generation.target: defective and defect-free RGB images with generated masks
generation.inputs: latent object/defect codes; normal images and few defective image-mask pairs for training
generation.conditioning: object category and learned defect category

claims.paraphrase: StyleGAN2 pretraining on normal images precedes training defect residual blocks and a defect mapping network. Mask-gated feature addition, image-mask discrimination and mode-seeking losses constrain visual content.
The second stage fixes the 23.2M-parameter backbone and trains 3.7M added parameters; these are author-reported counts, not measured resource use.

KID is evaluated using 5,000 generated defect images against the corresponding real defect category. Clustered LPIPS uses 1,000 outputs, assigned to nearest real-image clusters. Main results emphasize four hazelnut defects.

Each partition uses one-third of real defect images as base sets and the remaining two-thirds for classification tests. Hazelnut has 48 test images. ResNet-34 is trained on 4,000 generated images. Reported accuracies for three partitions are 83.33%, 81.25%, 81.25%.

Other object categories, implementation details, ablations and extreme one-/five-shot generation are deferred to a separate supplement. Main-paper classification does not establish segmentation performance or factory deployment.

No governing manufacturing process equation, calibrated physical variable or independent physical measurement is established in these main-paper methods and results. C0/V0 is a provisional process-physics code, not a claim that image metrics are absent.

design_limitations.issue: Generation-quality evaluation in Section 4.2 does not declare the classification holdout split used separately in Section 4.3. Do not silently assume a held-out KID reference set.
Random partitions within MVTec AD are not independent site/lot/tool validation; repeated partitions can share images and do not establish independent cohort replication.
Main paper defers implementation, other categories and extreme-shot experiments; complete main-PDF reading does not imply complete supplement reading.

open_questions: Acquire and fully review the separately linked supplement.
Resolve generation-quality reference split and scientific task-validator criteria.
Keep adapted execution distinct from unmodified author-command completion and independent reproduction.

records.title: Text-Guided Variational Image Generation for Industrial Anomaly Detection and Segmentation

generation.target: non-defective reference RGB images for anomaly-detector training
generation.inputs: one/five/full normal-image sets and target object keyword
generation.conditioning: WordNet-derived prompt, CLIP text/image embeddings and learned visual latent variance
generation.resolution_reported: not specified in reviewed main PDF

claims.paraphrase: WordNet prompt candidates are selected using CLIP. A VQGAN-derived generator estimates latent variance from augmented normal images; generated image sets are selected by text/image cosine similarity while the generator is updated.

The authors evaluate one-, five- and full-shot settings across PatchCore, CFLOW, Reverse Distillation and EfficientAD on MVTec AD, plus PatchCore experiments on BTAD and MVTec LOCO AD. Author text reports average improvements of 15.7%, 14.1% and 5.6%; the text does not justify pooling these as one metric across datasets.
The five displayed classes in the second row are selected for highest improvement; they are illustrative selected results, not an unbiased all-class aggregate.

The text-enabled ablation reports image-level 79.1 versus baseline 74.5, while pixel-level 96.9 is below baseline 97.0. Improvements are task- and setting-dependent, so a blanket all-metric gain is unsupported.

The visually inspected text retains a distance greater than 0.5 for prompt filtering; Eq. 6 divides a sum over M images by n; Table 2 reports LPIPS values in the hundreds without an explicit scale in the table. These are implementation/metric clarification questions, not corrections or demonstrated errors.

Visual latent variance, cosine selection and image losses do not provide manufacturing governing equations or independent physical metrology. The three offline datasets establish benchmark relevance, not calibrated process-condition or field qualification.

design_limitations.issue: Benchmarks across several datasets are not a documented external manufacturing site, lot or equipment qualification.
Selected best-improving classes must not be used as the all-class effect estimate.
The prompt ablation has different signs for image- and pixel-level change; generated-image count is not monotonically beneficial.
Equations, metric scaling and deferred supplement details need resolution before a faithful implementation or pooled metric comparison.

open_questions: Fully review separately linked supplement rather than infer content from bibliography page cross-references.
Recheck an immutable author release before any intent-to-run admission.
Clarify prompt-distance selection, Eq. 6 normalization, LPIPS scale, exact splits and dispersion definitions.

records.title: DefectFill: Realistic Defect Generation with Inpainting Diffusion Model for Visual Inspection

generation.target: defective RGB images on provided normal backgrounds and placement masks
generation.inputs: few defective image-mask pairs for fine-tuning; normal image and supplied mask for generation
generation.conditioning: learned defect token, object prompt, inpainting background and mask
generation.resolution_reported: not established in reviewed main PDF

claims.paraphrase: LoRA adapts text encoder and UNet attention. Defect-, object- and attention-based losses learn localized visual concepts. Sampling replaces background latents outside the mask; the selected result has the largest masked-region LPIPS among eight candidates.

One-third of defective image-mask pairs are used to learn defects, while remaining two-thirds masks are applied with normal images for synthesis. The main recipe uses SD2-inpainting, rank-8 LoRA and 50-step DDIM sampling.

Generation metrics use 1,000 images per defect category and aggregate by object across ten categories. Real defect images excluded from generator training form the metric reference. Baseline columns mix original-paper numbers, author reruns and filtered public generated datasets.

ResNet-34 classification and UNet localization are trained on generated images and evaluated on the remaining two-thirds real data. Capsule classification is 87.50%, and capsule localization AP is 0.75. These are author-reported benchmark results, not investigator reproduction.
LFS changes average reported KID from 28.485 to 25.947 and IC-LPIPS from 0.247 to 0.250. The authors explicitly note reduced effectiveness for global structural defects such as misalignment.

claims.location: Dataset paragraph and downstream test paragraph
claims.paraphrase: Masks from the same remaining-two-thirds partition are stated to be used in synthesis and that partition is also tested downstream. Exact sample and annotation lineage must be checked. This is an unresolved test-annotation exposure question, not a demonstrated image leak or invalidity verdict.

Visual semantic integration and latent masking do not constitute calibrated crack mechanics, material laws, process constraints or independent physical measurements. Main-paper offline MVTec results support visual inspection relevance only.

design_limitations.issue: Resolve source mask/sample lineage before classifying downstream testing as annotation-independent. Do not assume all use of held-out image masks is the same as image leakage.
Baseline columns have distinct provenance; copied results, author reruns and filtered public generated datasets are not a uniform experiment.
There are ten quantitative generation/localization categories but nine classification rows. Do not reuse a denominator of ten for classification.
External-image examples are qualitative; the explicit global-structural-defect limitation narrows suitability.
Eight-candidate selection has additional generation cost and may alter defect/severity distribution; neither calibrated severity nor end-to-end field throughput is established.

open_questions: Fully review separate supplement and inspect exact split/mask lineage in an attributable release if available.
Verify paper-linked author release separately from unofficial implementations.
Measure eight-candidate end-to-end generation cost under a declared profile and check calibrated defect/severity validity.
